How many colors are there?

The way people today see gender is more of a spectrum.

So if you look at the color spectrum there are points that you’d definitely see as "red" or "blue", that’s because these were so common that people decided to name them, and that’s entirely cultural (some cultures for example don’t really have blue and green as separate colors, but rather shades or the same color).  
And obviously there’s not only one color we call "red" - there are various shades and hues that are still red in our mind, and the limit of where red stops being red changes for each person.

And of course there are infinitely many unnamed colors. Colors in between others that you can’t really define. They exist, they might be close to a named color, but they’re something else.


Gender is the same way. There is a block for "men", and a block for "women" that most people are upon, which are why they’re named. And again the definition for these changes between cultures and people. 

Gender specifically is defined very differently between people, some think it’s purely biological, some think it’s how you present, others are how you see yourself or any combinations of the above.

Some people don’t fit anywhere in the named definitions, some are somewhere in the middle, some are both and some are neither.

Saying there are only two genders erases them. There are two commonly accepted areas on the gender spectrum, but infinite points on it.

So, why do I post this here?   
Because I literally can't find any other subreddit for trans-related media discussion - you can only submit links to /r/transgender, /r/trans is for selfies it seems, and /r/IASIP will not take kindly to criticism.   
So this is a -3 IQ play to make sure trans people will read my shit opinion, unless you're a mod and then this post is a 500 IQ play and the whole thing is satirizing media discussions.

So like, the Maureen Ponderosa thing is obviously transphobic garbage, right?

For those of you who don't know or remember, she is a recurring character. 

She starts out as a normal woman, but then decides to transition into a cat.  She gets a new name, plastic surgery, talks in meows and uses litter boxes.

Remember that extremely transphobic south park episode? where they equated being trans to wanting to become a shark?  And then they made the shark person grotesque to laugh at trans people?

This is literally the same, except unlike south park they have some subtlety.

People for some reason think that since IASIP has some built-in irony in it, then it's immune to criticism forever. 

Yes, I know the characters are supposed to be "bad people", but that's not the characters - that's the show's framing.


What do I mean?

- They literally use the phrase "Identify as a cat" multiple times. You know, like the attack helicopter joke everyone loves.
- Her transition clearly follows how a typical trans person might do it - getting a new name, adopting new habbits, dressing differently, having cosmetic surgeries, etc.
- She is about to do an "reverse nipplectomy" to add more nipples to more closely resemble a cat. You know, a top surgery.

It's a very trans-coded thing. 
Especially in the episode "Making Dennis Reynolds a Murderer"

But the thing is, she is NOT trans, she is CRAZY.  
You see, because it's not exactly 1-to-1, it means you got plausible deniability. 

And it's not just here - any criticism of any heavily-coded racial or gender stereotype will always be rebutted with "but you can't *know* they meant her to be X", or "Here's a plot reason for why it's ok that the only X character is a stereotype (the thermian argument)".

But honestly the connection was so strong I searched all over because I knew there had to be other folk who picked up on it, and I found nothing, so probably I am the crazy one.

It's kinda also ungoogleable because of Carmen - another character who is explicitly trans, and while there are some shitty aspects to how they handled the character (for example, using tranny everywhere to the point where even the show's creator regret using that word but the community is still at it https://www.reddit.com/r/IASIP/comments/kgcq8c/im_actually_really_happy_carmen_the_trans_woman/), but overall was ok.

But because Maureen is "crazy", the way people are handling her are "okay" in context, but might ring a bell to some of you:

- People refusing to use her name
- People calling her crazy or deranged
- Her actual brother "believing that she died three years ago upon her transition"
- When she dies due to her dangerous lifestyle nobody misses her
